question: If $P(a,b,c)$ and $Q(a+6,b-9,c+3)$ are two points on a directed line from $P$ to $Q$, obtain a simplest integral set of its direction ratios.
explanation: Step 1: Direction ratios of a line joining two points are proportional to the differences of their corresponding coordinates. Step 2: For the direction $P\to Q$, the differences are $$(a+6-a,\ b-9-b,\ c+3-c)=(6,-9,3).$$ Step 3: Thus, one set of direction ratios is $(6,-9,3)$. Step 4: Since any non-zero proportional set represents the same line direction, divide all three entries by their common factor $3$. This gives $(2,-3,1)$. Step 5: Therefore, a simplest integral set of direction ratios in the direction from $P$ to $Q$ is $$2,-3,1.$$ The opposite set $(-2,3,-1)$ would correspond to reversing the direction of the directed line.
